title: WhatsApp's iCloud Backup Alternative Rolls Out to Beta Users on iPhone
excerpt: WhatsApp is rolling out its first-party cloud backup service to some users on the beta version of the app for iOS, reports WABetaInfo. WhatsApp...
content_html:
Wednesday November 18, 2026 5:14 am PST by Tim Hardwick

WhatsApp is rolling out its first-party cloud backup service to some users on the beta version of the app for iOS, reports WABetaInfo.

WhatsApp cloud backup options in iOS beta (image: WABetaInfo)

The option is said to be appearing to some users on WhatsApp beta version 26.45.10.71, currently in TestFlight, providing users with an alternative to iCloud chat backup for the first time.

Code began appearing in beta versions of the app in July that suggested users would eventually be able to pick their preferred backup destination directly from the app's chat backup settings. iCloud remains the default, but the WhatsApp backup option differs in that it is fully end-to-end encrypted, and dedicated to chat backups only.

Under the plan, WhatsApp reportedly includes 2GB of free storage on its own end-to-end encrypted servers, and includes 100GB of storage to users on WhatsApp Plus, its paid subscription service costing $2.49 per month. With a Meta One subscription, users can receive up to 4TB depending on the plan they choose. WhatsApp already offers the backup option to users on Android.

WhatsApp has not announced when the feature will be available to everyone, but its availability in the beta suggests it could roll out more broadly in the coming weeks.
